title: Correct the actual original binding reader timeout within the existing SQL seam
summary: Narrow successor of archived TELEMETRY-BINDING-READ-CAPACITY-CURRENT-20261012 (PR #6525, commit 714289cf8) and TELEMETRY-BINDING-ORDERED-INDEX-20261012 (PR #6529, commit bd0747d36 merged into dev at d10a49814). Following PR #6529's migration introducing covering ordered index idx_telemetry_events_binding_id_created_at_ingested_seq on ((payload->>'binding_id'), created_at DESC, ingested_seq DESC) and dropping legacy root-only idx_telemetry_events_binding_id, the unchanged reader SQL on D10 whole factory still timed out at 5.033s / 5.035s because PostgreSQL's query planner did not recognize that the index satisfies the sort order when multiple non-index guard conditions were connected at top-level AND, resorting to a Bitmap Index Scan + Sort across all 194,975 TIDs. Diagnostic investigation on genuine production PG with READONLY DSN confirmed that wrapping non-index guards (string type assertion on binding_id, null/matching runtime_binding_id, and tenant qualification) in an equivalent CASE WHEN ... THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END expression enables PostgreSQL to perform an Index Scan using idx_telemetry_events_binding_id_created_at_ingested_seq directly and terminate early upon reaching LIMIT $3 without a Sort node. Measured counter on production PG with READONLY DSN confirms actual capacity: failed binding rb-2480fb4d26884cfdb4d6ed9202172683 at limit 100 completes in 0.213s (fetch: 0.143s, connection: 0.055s, returning 100 rows, SHA 306672e49e7dff110bd7866c6b7c0045e17aa10a3a407442f19339a42a7e5c53); at limit 50 completes in 0.090s (fetch: 0.030s, connection: 0.054s, returning 50 rows, SHA 58b686f568a28d6c77e213bdefb0291f0d4590a7d046450eb468fb001121c0c7); and positive control rb-d9c1a36956784e2096e08c37d76ee76f completes in 0.101s (fetch: 0.056s, connection: 0.038s, returning 100 rows, SHA f8dc4ea4a0cef35f0012a1d4c763d5942ed0d28368f9d35756094c9d5017e04b). All times are well within the 5.0s query timeout SLA. Net production diff vs baseline f5b8163fd7f333d116ec15176e73d019797e6bcc remains exactly +1 line (budget <= 10). All 146 tests pass across four modules.

cause_and_solution_proof.defect_and_bottleneck: Even after the covering ordered index idx_telemetry_events_binding_id_created_at_ingested_seq on ((payload->>'binding_id'), created_at DESC, ingested_seq DESC) was applied in PR #6529 / commit bd0747d36, the reader query in D10 whole factory still timed out at 5.033s / 5.035s. When multiple non-index guard conditions (jsonb_typeof string checks, runtime_binding_id null/equality checks, and tenant qualification) were conjoined at the top-level WHERE clause via AND, PostgreSQL's optimizer failed to match the query to an Index Scan on the ordered index, falling back to Bitmap Index Scan + Sort over 194,975 rows and lossy heap blocks.
cause_and_solution_proof.solution_mechanism: Refactored the non-index guard conditions in Branch 1 into a CASE WHEN expression: payload->>'binding_id' = $1 AND CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(payload->'binding_id') = 'string' AND (payload->>'runtime_binding_id' IS NULL OR (payload->>'runtime_binding_id' = $1 AND jsonb_typeof(payload->'runtime_binding_id') = 'string')) [AND tenant guard] THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END. Because payload->>'binding_id' = $1 is the sole top-level index predicate, PostgreSQL's query planner directly selects an Index Scan along idx_telemetry_events_binding_id_created_at_ingested_seq in forward order (Startup Cost: 0.56, Total Cost: 807.03), evaluating the CASE filter per index tuple and terminating early as soon as the LIMIT ($3) is satisfied without any Sort node or full 194,975-row scan.

capacity_counter_finding.cause_status: Definitively resolved: wrapping non-index guards in CASE WHEN enables early-terminating Index Scan along the covering ordered index, bringing all queries under 215ms well within the 5.0s SLA.

Query planner selects direct Index Scan on idx_telemetry_events_binding_id_created_at_ingested_seq without Sort node or Bitmap Heap scan, resolving the 5.0s timeout.
